title: Number Bases: Binary and Other Bases
seo_title: Number Bases – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count in base two and other bases; convert numbers from base ten to other bases and from other bases to base ten; add and subtract in base two. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on number bases: base two (binary), base three, four, five and eight, converting to and from base ten, and binary addition and subtraction. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Base b place values: 1, b, b², b³
key_sub: Divide by the base, read the remainders upwards.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In base ten the place values are 1, 10, 100, 1,000. In base five they are 1, 5, 25, 125. In base two they are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.
  • A digit in base b is always less than b: base five uses only 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4.
  • To change base ten to another base, divide by the base again and again and read the remainders from the bottom up.

Examples

Example

234₅ to base ten

2 × 25 + 3 × 5 + 4

Answer: 69

Example

29 to base four

29 = 1 × 16 + 3 × 4 + 1

Answer: 131₄

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using a digit as big as the baseThere is no digit 5 in base five.
Reading remainders downwardsRead them from the last one up.
Multiplying by 10 for every placeMultiply by the base, not by 10.

faq.q: Why is base two used in computers?
faq.a: Electric switches are either on (1) or off (0).

items.q: Change 24 to a binary number (base two).
items.e: Divide by 2 again and again: 24 ÷ 2 = 12 remainder 0; 12 ÷ 2 = 6 remainder 0; 6 ÷ 2 = 3 remainder 0; 3 ÷ 2 = 1 remainder 1; 1 ÷ 2 = 0 remainder 1. Read the remainders from the bottom up: 11000₂.
